activities.name: Teatro Colón Guided Architecture Tour
activities.description: Explore one of the world's top five opera houses — the magnificent Teatro Colón, a French Renaissance masterpiece with a legendary acoustic profile, seven tiers of red velvet and gold, and a backstage that has hosted Caruso, Callas, and Nureyev. A landmark of South American cultural grandeur.
activities.duration_note: Book in advance — tours sell out on weekends

activities.name: Traditional Milonga Tango Hall Night
activities.description: Step into an authentic Buenos Aires milonga — a late-night social tango hall where locals dance until 4 AM, lessons flow into social dancing, and the entire room operates on a silent code of glances and nods. The real tango has nothing to do with tourist shows; this is where it lives.
activities.duration_note: Milongas typically start after midnight and run until dawn — dress smartly

activities.name: San Telmo Sunday Antique Market
activities.description: Wander the cobblestoned streets of San Telmo on Sunday as the entire neighborhood transforms into a sprawling open-air antique market — hundreds of vendors selling silver mate sets, vintage maps, leather goods, and art, with impromptu tango dancers performing at every corner.
activities.duration_note: Sundays only — free entry. Keep phone secured; pickpockets active in crowded tourist zones

activities.name: Estancia Day — Asado, Horses & Gaucho Culture
activities.description: Spend a full day at a historic Pampas cattle estancia — riding through open grasslands on Criollo horses with gaucho guides, watching rope and boleadora demonstrations, listening to folk music around the fire, and finishing with an extensive traditional asado feast with Malbec under the open sky.
activities.location: San Antonio de Areco, Buenos Aires Province
activities.duration_note: Full-day experience including all meals, transport from Buenos Aires, and activities

activities.name: Plaza de Mayo, Casa Rosada & Recoleta Cemetery Walk
activities.description: Trace Argentina's turbulent political and cultural history — from the iconic pink Casa Rosada balcony of Eva Perón and the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo to the elaborate above-ground mausoleum city of Recoleta Cemetery, where Argentine presidents, generals, and Evita herself are entombed.

activities.name: Ojo de Bife & Provoleta at Don Julio Parrilla
activities.description: Dine at Don Julio — the world-renowned Buenos Aires parrilla in Palermo — for a perfectly charcoal-grilled ojo de bife (ribeye) sourced from grass-fed Pampas cattle, with a bubbling provoleta grilled cheese starter and a bottle of single-vineyard Malbec. The definitive Argentine steak experience.
activities.duration_note: Reservations essential — book 2+ weeks in advance for Don Julio

activities.name: Choripán at the Costanera Sur
activities.description: Join the Sunday ritual of Buenos Aires families at the Costanera Sur riverside strip — eating a fat chorizo sandwich (choripán) from a smoky street carrito, loaded with chimichurri and salsa criolla, watching the brown Río de la Plata stretch to the horizon. Argentina's greatest $4 meal.

activities.name: Florería Atlántico Speakeasy & Tres Monos Cocktails
activities.description: Enter Florería Atlántico through a working flower shop, descend to one of the world's top-ranked underground bars — a homage to South Atlantic immigration waves, with exceptional cocktails built on vermouth, gin, and regional botanicals. Then visit Tres Monos in Chacarita for avant-garde mixology in a tiny, electric space.
activities.duration_note: Reservations required at Florería Atlántico. Both venues among South America's best bars

activities.name: La Viruta Tango Club
activities.description: Dance late into the night at La Viruta — one of Buenos Aires' most beloved tango clubs in Palermo, running tango and folklore classes from 9 PM before the social dancing floor opens around midnight to a mix of locals and travelers in a convivial, genuinely welcoming atmosphere.
activities.duration_note: Entry ~COP 5,800 ARS. Classes start at 9 PM, social dancing from midnight

activities.name: Perito Moreno Glacier Minitrekking
activities.description: Strap on crampons and trek directly over the surface of the Perito Moreno Glacier — one of the world's only advancing glaciers — walking through deep blue ice channels, around towering seracs, and to the edge of crevasses above the thundering turquoise meltwater lake below.
activities.location: Los Glaciares National Park, Santa Cruz
activities.duration_note: Must book 2–3 months in advance — strict daily capacity caps. Patagonian weather changes hourly — pack waterproof layers regardless of forecast

activities.name: Laguna de los Tres — Fitz Roy Trek
activities.description: Hike one of the most iconic trails in Patagonia — a self-guided full-day trek from El Chaltén through lenga beech forest and boulder fields to the glacial Laguna de los Tres, where the sheer granite spires of Mount Fitz Roy rise directly from the water's edge in an impossibly dramatic composition.
activities.duration_note: Free — El Chaltén is the only Argentine national park with no entry fee. Start early; afternoon winds make the final ascent brutal

activities.name: Beagle Channel Navigation Cruise
activities.description: Sail the Beagle Channel — where Darwin made his historic observations — past rugged rocky islands to the historic Les Éclaireurs Lighthouse, sea lion colonies hauled out on rocky outcrops, and large colonies of Magellanic and Gentoo penguins at the bottom of the world.

activities.name: Tierra del Fuego National Park Hike
activities.description: Walk coastal sub-Antarctic forest trails inside the world's southernmost national park — the symbolic end of the Pan-American Highway — through ancient Nothofagus beech groves, along the Beagle Channel shoreline, and to Lapataia Bay, where a simple sign marks 'The End of the World.'

activities.name: Circuito Chico Scenic Bike Ride
activities.description: Cycle the classic Circuito Chico loop around Bariloche — a 60-kilometer route past the impossibly blue Lake Nahuel Huapi, through Arrayán myrtle forests, and up to the Cerro Campanario summit viewpoint — considered one of the most beautiful lakeside cycling routes in South America.
activities.duration_note: Price covers bike rental for the day

activities.name: Cordero Patagónico & King Crab Dinner
activities.description: Taste the two great proteins of the far south — Cordero Patagónico, whole Patagonian lamb slow-roasted over iron cross-pits on open coals until falling apart, at a regional estancia or lodge, then in Ushuaia indulge in freshly caught Centolla (King Crab) pulled from the icy Beagle Channel waters.

activities.name: Cervecería Patagonia & La Cervecería Chaltén
activities.description: Sample Argentina's finest craft beer culture — Cervecería Patagonia in Bariloche for its lakeside setting and flagship ales, or La Cervecería Chaltén in El Chaltén where hikers gather post-trail to swap stories over cold IPAs and stouts with the Fitz Roy massif glowing outside the window.
activities.duration_note: No cover charge at either venue — casual hiker-friendly atmosphere

activities.name: Uco Valley Premium Winery & Andes Pairing Tour
activities.description: Tour the extraordinary architectural wineries of the Uco Valley — gravity-fed modern cellars backed by 6,000-meter Andean peaks at 1,000 meters altitude — with a multi-course wine pairing lunch showcasing high-altitude Malbec, Cabernet Franc, and Torrontés matched to regional ingredients.
activities.duration_note: Private remís (chauffeured car) strongly recommended — do not drive between tastings. Wineries spread across far-flung valleys

activities.name: Chacras de Coria Boutique Winery Bike Tour
activities.description: Rent a vintage cruiser bicycle to navigate the shaded tree-lined lanes of Chacras de Coria in Luján de Cuyo — pedaling between boutique family-owned bodegas for cellar-door tastings of old-vine Malbec and estate Bonarda, stopping at local almacenes for empanadas between wineries.
activities.location: Chacras de Coria, Luján de Cuyo, Mendoza

activities.name: Mount Aconcagua Base Area Hike
activities.description: Drive Route 7 up through the dramatic Horcones Valley to Confluencia base area beneath the highest peak in the Western Hemisphere — Aconcagua at 6,961 meters — for a day hike with staggering views of the South Wall and surrounding Andean giants without the commitment of a full summit expedition.
activities.duration_note: Price is park entry fee only. Altitude above 3,000m — acclimatize in Mendoza first

activities.name: Mendoza River Whitewater Rafting
activities.description: Battle Class III–IV rapids on the glacially fed Mendoza River through the rugged Potrerillos canyon — a rush of cold Andean snowmelt charging through dramatic desert rock walls, with professional local guides navigating the most technical sections at high water in spring and early summer.
activities.duration_note: Best water levels September through November (snowmelt season)

activities.name: Cacheuta Mountain Canyon Thermal Pools
activities.description: Soak in naturally heated thermal pools built directly into a spectacular desert mountain canyon wall at Termas Cacheuta — a series of pools at different temperatures carved into the orange rock face, with the Mendoza River rushing through the gorge below and the Andes rising on all sides.

activities.name: Empanadas Mendocinas & Chivo Asado
activities.description: Taste the culinary soul of Cuyo — freshly baked Empanadas Mendocinas stuffed with spiced beef, hard-boiled egg, and olives in wood-fired clay ovens, followed by Chivo (whole roasted goat) slow-cooked on an open pit. The simple, bold flavors of the Andean piedmont at its best.

activities.name: Arístides Villanueva Bar Strip & Malbec Wine Bar
activities.description: Walk Mendoza's most energetic nightlife street — Arístides Villanueva, lined with open-air bars and live music terraces — then settle in at The Vines Wine Bar or Chachingo for premium single-vineyard Malbec pours from small producers who don't export, in a city where exceptional wine costs less than a coffee elsewhere.

activities.name: Iguazú Falls National Park Boardwalk Trails
activities.description: Walk the extensive upper and lower boardwalk circuits through UNESCO-listed Iguazú Falls — 275 individual cascades stretching 2.7 kilometers wide, the world's largest waterfall system — with the final walkway extending directly above the roaring Devil's Throat where 1.5 million liters per second plunge into white oblivion.
activities.duration_note: Visit both the Argentine and Brazilian sides for the full perspective — separate entry tickets required for each country

activities.name: Great Adventure Speedboat Under the Falls
activities.description: Board a twin-engine inflatable speedboat for a full-throttle charge up the Iguazú River canyon directly underneath the thundering walls of the falls — emerging completely soaked inside a roaring curtain of white water and mist in one of the most exhilarating five minutes in South American adventure travel.
activities.duration_note: Waterproof everything — you will be completely drenched

activities.name: Quebrada de Humahuaca Colored Canyon Road Trip
activities.description: Drive through the spectacular UNESCO-listed Quebrada de Humahuaca — a 155-kilometer canyon of multi-layered sedimentary rock glowing in reds, purples, greens, and ochres — visiting the indigenous villages of Tilcara, Humahuaca, and Purmamarca, each with active ceremonial traditions and artisan markets.
activities.duration_note: Price covers car rental for the day. Altitude above 2,500m — buy sorojchi pills in Jujuy pharmacy or chew coca leaves available at markets

activities.name: Salinas Grandes High Altitude Salt Flat
activities.description: Stand on the vast, blindingly white expanse of the Salinas Grandes salt flat at 3,450 meters above sea level on the puna plateau — a surreal, perfectly level white canvas bordered by the multicolored Andes, where perspective tricks and mirror reflections after rain create infinite photographic possibilities.
activities.duration_note: Guide fee. Altitude 3,450m — acclimatize in Salta or Jujuy for 24hrs first. Bring strong UV sunglasses and sunscreen — reflection is intense

activities.name: Traditional Peña Folklore Night in Salta
activities.description: Sit at a candlelit table in a traditional Salteña peña — a folklore music hall where local artists perform chacarera, zamba, and Andean folk songs, patrons spontaneously sing along, couples dance between tables, and the night unfolds over plates of locro stew and glasses of Torrontés wine.
activities.duration_note: Entry includes show. La Casona del Molino on Balcarce Street is the most acclaimed venue

activities.name: Locro, Humitas & Salteña Empanadas
activities.description: Taste the Andean north's most distinctive comfort foods — Locro, a slow-cooked hearty stew of corn, white beans, and pork that has been simmering in northwest Argentina for centuries, alongside sweet Humitas (corn paste wrapped in husks) and small, juicy, spiced Salteña empanadas baked in wood-fired ovens.

activities.name: Balcarce Street Peña Crawl — Salta
activities.description: Stroll Balcarce Street — Salta's vibrant folklore nightlife corridor — moving between traditional peñas and live music bars where the sound of chacarera guitar and bombo drum spills out onto the cobblestones, sharing bottles of local Torrontés white wine and craft Kolsch beers into the cool Andean night.
